pile.scheme:
Q1: 20 (1).
Q2: 20% of $60 = $12 (1); $60 - $12 = $48 (1).
Q3: 60% (1).
Q4: B, $75 (1). Method (2): the 50% increase is on $100, giving $150 (1); the 50% decrease is on the new price $150, so $75 is taken off, giving $75 (1). The two percentages are of different amounts, so they do not cancel. Saying +50% and -50% cancel gets no method marks.
Q5: 10% of $2,000 = $200 (1); $2,200 (1).
Q6: $45 / 5 = $9 a part (1); Ana $18, Ben $27 (1).
pile.title: Mathematics: Percentages and Money

patterns.idea: Thinks 50% is always a fixed $50 amount
patterns.reteach: Reteach that a percentage is always of a particular amount, showing that 50% of $100 is $50 but 50% of $20 is $10 and 50% of $150 is $75.

patterns.idea: Thinks the same percent up then down cancels back to the start
patterns.reteach: Reteach that the second change is worked out from the new price, tracking $100 up 50% to $150 and then taking 50% of $150, which is $75 off and leaves $75.

patterns.idea: Chose $100 with no working shown, so the reason is not yet known
patterns.reteach: Ask Lo first to explain how he got $100, prompting 'What did you work out 50% of at each step?', before assuming he shares either of the other ideas.

patterns.tomorrow: First, ask Lo to talk through his $100 answer while checking what the rest of the class think, then model successive percentage changes with a tracker that records the new base before each step. Practise problems where students must say 'percent of what?' before calculating, using different starting prices and percentages that are not both 50%.

next_exam.text: A jacket costs $80. Its price rises by 25%, then falls by 25%. Find its final price and explain why it is not $80.
Work out 50% of $40, 50% of $90, and 50% of $150. Explain in one sentence why the answers are not all the same amount.
A bike costs $200. Its price increases by 10%, then decreases by 10%. Calculate the final price, showing what amount each percentage is worked out from.

questions.text: A jacket costs $60. In a sale it is 20% off. What is the sale price? Show your working.

A product costs $100. Its price increases by 50%, then decreases by 50%. What is its final price? Circle one answer and explain your thinking. A $100 — back to the original price B $75 — lower than the original price C $50 — half the original price D $150 — higher than the original price
A salary of $2,000 a month rises by 10%. What is the new salary?
Share $45 between Ana and Ben in the ratio 2 : 3.
